findings.issue_text: [BUG] The claim that 'the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false: Django querysets raise ValueError ('Negative indexing is not supported.') when sliced with a negative start offset. When enable_advanced_features=True and a request arrives with a negative-offset cursor, queryset[start_offset:stop] raises ValueError and the audit-logs endpoint returns a 500 instead of a result page; the entire 'advanced pagination' path is unexercisable.

[BUG] The modified BasePaginator.get_result unclamps offsets when cursor.is_prev, so any client-crafted cursor carrying a negative offset produces a negative slice on every existing paginator (DateTimePaginator included), which Django rejects. Any user of any DateTimePaginator-based endpoint can send a cursor with is_prev=true and negative offset and crash the request with a ValueError/500 — a regression on all endpoints sharing BasePaginator, not just audit logs.

[BUG] The code evaluates organization_context.member.has_global_access without guaranteeing the requesting user is a member of the organization (superusers hitting the control-silo endpoint for an org they don't belong to get member=None), and organization_context is not a name established in this endpoint's get() scope. A superuser or org admin request on an organization where the user has no OrganizationMember row (or where organization_context is simply not bound in this method) raises AttributeError/NameError and returns a 500 on the audit-log listing before pagination ever runs.

[BUG] self.paginate(..., enable_advanced_features=True) forwards a keyword that the base endpoint's paginate() signature does not accept (it builds paginator kwargs from its descriptor, not via **kwargs passthrough to paginator_cls). The optimized branch raises TypeError at runtime the first time an authorized admin passes optimized_pagination=true, meaning the feature can never be exercised successfully as written.

[BUG] The optimized path passes `enable_advanced_features=True` as a kwarg to `self.paginate(...)`, but the paginate helper does not forward unknown kwargs to the paginator constructor, so this either raises TypeError or is silently dropped, disabling the negative-offset feature the paginator branch promises. Admin requests with optimized_pagination=true hit an unhandled TypeError (500) or the paginator runs with enable_advanced_features=False, making the new code path a silent no-op.

[BUG] Django ORM querysets do not support negative slice bounds — `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start_offset raises ValueError ("Negative indexing is not allowed"), so the advanced negative-offset path crashes instead of paginating. Any cursor crafted with a negative offset on the optimized path returns a 500 instead of results; the comment claiming 'the Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is factually wrong.

[BUG] `organization_context.member.has_global_access` dereferences `member` without a None check; a superuser or user without membership in the organization has `member` set to None, raising AttributeError. Superusers calling GET /organizations/<slug>/auditlogs/ without org membership get a 500 AttributeError on the attribute lookup that happens before the is_superuser short-circuit can help (member is evaluated even when is_superuser is True because of attribute access order in the expression — actually `or` short-circuits, but any non-superuser org member context where member is None crashes).

[BUG] The base BasePaginator.get_result now clamps offsets with `max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, but for prev cursors a negative offset passes through unchanged and hits Django's negative-slice ValueError, an edge case no section addresses and no test covers. A client sending a crafted prev cursor with negative offset on any DateTimePaginator endpoint gets a 500; the diff adds this code path with zero tests exercising negative or prev-cursor offsets.

[ADVISORY] The entire OptimizedCursorPaginator class — a new non-trivial paginator with its own boundary logic — ships with no tests anywhere in the diff (no spec/test files present), leaving get_item_key flooring/ceiling, prev-cursor trimming, and reverse behavior unverified. The next refactor of build_cursor or Cursor semantics silently breaks admin audit-log pagination with no failing test to catch it; uncovered behaviors include the prev-cursor duplicate-filtering branch and the has_results cursor construction.

[ADVISORY] The offset-clamping logic is duplicated and drifting between BasePaginator.get_result and OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result (`max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` appears verbatim in both), a parallel hand-maintained pair that will diverge on the next fix. A future fix to negative-offset handling applied to one copy leaves the other broken; extraction to a shared helper deletes the duplicated block and the drift risk.

[ADVISORY] The new behavior is gated on a raw query parameter `optimized_pagination=true` with no API schema, feature flag, or options entry, and silently falls back to the old paginator for non-privileged users with no error or signal. Clients cannot discover the capability, non-admin users passing the flag get silently different pagination semantics (no 4xx), and operators cannot disable the negative-offset path without a code deploy if it misbehaves.

[ADVISORY] Cursor now accepts negative offsets by design, but cursor construction/serialization round-trip for negative offsets is not validated anywhere, so the deserialization of a cursor whose offset was negative may behave differently from what the paginator assumes. Clients round-tripping an advanced paginator cursor with negative offset through serialize_cursor/decode may get a clamped or corrupted offset, producing duplicated or skipped rows in audit-log navigation with no test to define the contract.

[BUG] The BasePaginator slicing change passes a negative start offset to Django queryset slicing, which raises ValueError, not 'handled boundary conditions'. When cursor.is_prev is true with a negative cursor.offset, `queryset[start_offset:stop]` raises "QuerySet slice indices must be integers or None"/negative-index ValueError, returning a 500 on every backward-pagination request whose offset goes negative.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on self.key of the item, but this paginator is instantiated with order_by='-datetime', so value is a datetime and int(math.floor(datetime)) raises TypeError. Any admin request with optimized_pagination=true crashes with a TypeError 500 instead of returning audit log rows.

[BUG] When cursor.value is falsy, the code sets cursor_value = 0 and calls build_queryset(0, ...), producing a queryset filtered on key 0 rather than an unfiltered first page. An empty cursor value (e.g., Cursor(0, 0, 0) constructed when cursor is None) filters audit logs to datetime epoch, returning zero rows for the first page of the optimized path.

[ADVISORY] The feature is gated on a raw `optimized_pagination=true` query parameter plus an inline superuser check, which is neither part of the stated intent (pagination performance) nor configurable, and duplicates branch logic instead of a flag. Operators cannot disable or roll out the new code path without a deploy; the performance intent is served by an unrelated auth-gated hidden parameter that no requirement traces to, and the is_superuser check silently changes behavior for admins only.

[BUG] `organization_context.member.has_global_access` assumes organization_context.member is non-None, but for superusers or service users accessing an org they're not a member of, member is None and this raises AttributeError. Requests that previously succeeded via the standard paginator now 500 during the permission check for the gate itself, breaking audit log listing for non-member superusers.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is a ~70-line copy of BasePaginator.get_result with two divergent branches, creating a parallel hand-maintained duplicate of core pagination logic. Future fixes to the base paginator (e.g., the is_prev trimming bug present in the copy's `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` comparison, which compares against offset rather than the actual start_offset used) will not propagate; the two implementations have already drifted within this diff.

[BUG] The prev-page dedup branch checks `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` but results were sliced starting at start_offset (possibly negative), so the length comparison against the unadjusted offset is wrong for the negative-offset path. On backward pagination with negative offsets, the last result is not trimmed when it should be, or is trimmed when it shouldn't be, yielding duplicated/missing rows at page boundaries.

[ADVISORY] The only change to Cursor is a comment claiming negative offsets are a supported 'performance optimization'; no validation or type change accompanies it, so the comment documents behavior the class does not implement. The comment asserts safety of a mechanism that actually crashes at the ORM layer (negative slicing ValueError), misleading future maintainers into extending the broken pattern; it is work not traceable to any requirement in the PR intent.

[BUG] Django QuerySet slicing with a negative start offset raises ValueError ('Negative indexing is not supported'), so the 'advanced negative offset' path crashes instead of paginating. Any admin client sending an optimized_pagination=true cursor with a negative offset gets a 500 from the audit log endpoint; the comment 'the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false — Django explicitly forbids it, and unlike Python lists, queryset[-5:100] never returns tail rows.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on the key attribute, which raises TypeError when the paginator is used with datetime ordering (the audit log endpoint orders by -datetime), since datetime objects support neither __floor__ nor numeric comparison to ints. The first request through the optimized path (any superuser with optimized_pagination=true) crashes in get_item_key during build_cursor, returning a 500 — the feature has no working configuration at all, and the unit-looking copy from OffsetPaginator's int-key logic was never adapted for DateTimePaginator's data type.

[BUG] The prev-cursor trimming branch compares len(results) == offset + limit + extra using the original cursor.offset while the slice was taken from start_offset, so the off-by-one trim fires at the wrong length whenever start_offset != offset (negative or clamped offsets). On a prev traversal with a clamped/negative offset, results[:-1] strips a real row or fails to strip the boundary duplicate, silently duplicating or dropping an audit log row at page boundaries for clients using the optimized paginator.

[BUG] The base Paginator.get_result change clamps negative offsets to 0 for forward cursers but passes negative offsets through unchanged for is_prev cursers, and that is_prev branch still feeds the negative offset into queryset[offset:stop], which Django rejects. The shared base paginator used by DateTimePaginator now has a negative-offset code path that can only ever raise ValueError; the clamp is also a silent behavior change for any pre-existing caller that somehow passed a negative offset (previously a deterministic error, now silently page-one results on forward cursers).

[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is a near-verbatim copy of the existing DateTimePaginator/BasePaginator get_result with hand-applied edits, creating two parallel implementations of the same pagination state machine that will drift. Future fixes to cursor edge cases in the base get_result (the prev-trim and reverse logic already subtly differs here) will not reach the optimized copy, so admin audit-log pages and normal pages will disagree on results after the next paginator bugfix.

[ADVISORY] A materially different pagination behavior is gated on a raw query param (optimized_pagination=true) combined with an is_superuser/global-access check, with no feature flag, options entry, or versioned API surface. The new path cannot be disabled without a code deploy once a superuser client starts relying on it, and non-superuser org admins silently get the old paginator for the same request shape — an authorization-dependent response-shape divergence that API consumers will experience as inconsistent pagination semantics with no way to roll back via config.

[ADVISORY] The 'advanced' negative-offset branch exists only behind a constructor flag set from a superuser query param, and its only effect is to route around the max(0, offset) clamp added to the base class — a security-relevant bound bypass dressed as a performance optimization, with comments asserting safety ('permissions are checked at the queryset level') that the diff does not establish. The next maintainer reading 'Performance optimization' has no in-code evidence for why negative offsets are safe or what they're for; the branch provides zero measured performance benefit (the query is unchanged for non-negative offsets) while adding a bypassable boundary, so it should be deleted rather than kept as dead-weight risk.

[BUG] The modified BasePaginator.get_result silently clamps negative offsets instead of erroring, changing pagination behavior for every existing paginator beyond the PR's stated 'audit log performance' intent. A client sending a cursor with a crafted negative offset, which previously failed, now receives valid results from max(0, offset), i.e. the start of the dataset — data a client should not have been able to reach, and a behavior change to all endpoints using this base class with no human acceptance recorded.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result slices the queryset with a negative start_offset when enable_advanced_features is set, and Django ORM raises ValueError('Negative indices are not allowed') on negative slicing of a queryset. The comment 'the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false: any superuser request with optimized_pagination=true and a negative-offset cursor returns a 500 instead of a page of audit logs — the happy path in the PR cannot execute at all.

[BUG] The prev-page dedup branch uses len(results) == offset + limit + extra, which is wrong when offset was negative (or clamped), since len(results) can never be negative — the length comparison will never match for negative-offset cursors. When a prev cursor with a value equal to the first item's key is used alongside the negative-offset path, results[:1] is skipped but the elif fallback never fires, so callers receive one too many or one missing row per page with no error to detect it.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls int(math.floor(value) if ... else math.ceil(value)) on the key attribute, which for this endpoint's key (datetime from order_by='-datetime') raises TypeError because math.floor does not accept a datetime. Every optimized-path request crashes with a TypeError (500), meaning the feature added by this diff cannot serve any audit-log page — the DateTimePaginator path it replaced handled datetimes correctly.

[ADVISORY] The endpoint's objective silently drifted from 'faster pagination of audit logs' to a dual-mode API gated on a raw query param and an authorization check, with no feature flag, options entry, or documented client contract for the new mode. Operators cannot disable the optimized path without a code deploy, and any superuser or global-access member who passes optimized_pagination=true gets a materially different (and, per the crashes above, broken) paginator — a silent public-surface change no review accepted.

[BUG] The gating expression organization_context.member.has_global_access is evaluated without confirming organization_context is non-None, and references an attribute chain that is not established elsewhere in this endpoint, so requests where organization_context is None raise AttributeError before the queryset is ever returned. Non-superuser GETs to /organizations/<slug>/auditlogs/ return a 500 when organization_context is unset, where the pre-diff code path served the DateTimePaginator page normally.

[ADVISORY] Cursor.__init__ accepts any int offset with no lower-bound validation, and the diff's comments frame negative offsets as an intended feature while nothing downstream sanitizes client-supplied cursor offsets. The unvalidated negative offset becomes client-controlled input that reaches queryset slicing; any paginator adopting the 'advanced' path exposes out-of-bounds reads, and future maintainers reading the comment will assume negativity was reviewed and safe.

[BUG] The base paginator's prev-cursor branch (`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`) allows negative offsets for ANY client, bypassing the admin/superuser gate the endpoint claims enforces advanced pagination. Sentry cursor payloads are merely base64-encoded, not signed, so any org member can forge a prev cursor with a negative offset against the default DateTimePaginator path and exercise the 'admin-only' advanced pagination behavior the endpoint's `enable_advanced` check is supposed to gate; on Django this path either returns data at attacker-chosen arbitrary negative offsets or blows up with ValueError/AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported'), producing a 500 on an org-scoped endpoint.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator slices the queryset with an unclamped negative start offset (`start_offset = cursor.offset`), which Django's ORM rejects for negative slice bounds. Any admin who sends a cursor with a negative offset (or a crafted/overrun cursor) gets an unhandled ValueError/AssertionError from the ORM slice `queryset[-N:stop]`, returning a 500 from the audit log endpoint instead of results — a client-controlled crash primitive on a control-silo endpoint reachable by every org admin via `?optimized_pagination=true`.

[ADVISORY] A new code path (optimized paginator plus admin-gated advanced features) is toggled by a raw, unvalidated query-string parameter `optimized_pagination` with no feature flag, options entry, or allowlist of supported values. Operators cannot disable or roll out the optimized path without a code deploy, and any unauthenticated string value (only the exact literal 'true' matches, everything else silently selects the legacy path) makes behavior depend on client-supplied routing; a misconfigured client or probe toggles a lightly-tested pagination implementation on a security-sensitive audit-log endpoint. Author's counterargument is that the admin check still gates execution, which is true for privilege but does not address the deploy/rollback or untested-path exposure.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result slices the queryset with a client-controlled negative offset (queryset[start_offset:stop] with start_offset < 0), which Django ORM queryset slicing rejects with ValueError/AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported'), so the request crashes with a 500. Any superuser or org member with global access who passes ?optimized_pagination=true with a cursor containing a negative offset gets an unhandled 500 on the audit-log endpoint; since cursor.offset comes straight from the request query param, this is trivially triggered and cannot be disabled without a code deploy.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil to self.key's value, but the endpoint passes order_by='-datetime', so value is a datetime and int(math.floor(datetime)) raises TypeError, crashing every previous-page request on the optimized path. When enable_advanced_features is on and the client follows a 'prev' cursor (cursor.is_prev with results), get_result calls get_item_key(results[0], for_prev=True) and the endpoint returns a 500 instead of the previous page of audit logs.

[ADVISORY] The prev-dedup logic compares len(results) == offset + limit + extra using the raw (possibly negative) offset while the slice used start_offset, so the two offsets disagree and the boundary-trim branch results[:-1] silently drops the wrong element or never fires. Admins paging backwards through audit logs on the optimized path get a duplicated or missing row at page boundaries — silent data mispagination rather than a crash, and the drift between the two offset computations makes the next change to this paginator harder to reason about.

[ADVISORY] A new paginator behavior is gated on the raw query param optimized_pagination=true plus a permission check, with no feature flag, options entry, or accompanying test, so it cannot be disabled or gradually rolled out without a code deploy. Operators shipping this get an all-at-once behavior change on a high-volume audit-log endpoint; any of the crash modes above becomes immediately reachable by any global-access user with no kill switch.

[ADVISORY] The base BasePaginator.get_result slicing logic was changed (start_offset = max(0, offset) when not is_prev) for all existing DateTimePaginator/OrgCursorPaginator callers, altering stop computation for negative-offset cursors on every endpoint that uses this base class, not just the new optimized path. Every existing paginated endpoint's slice bounds change whenever a client crafts a negative-offset cursor; previously offset+limit+extra, now 0+limit+extra, so a crafted cursor silently shifts the returned window — a cross-endpoint behavior change shipped inside a 'performance' PR with no test covering the base-class change.

[BUG] The OptimizedCursorPaginator's 'advanced' negative-offset path slices a Django queryset with a negative start index, which Django rejects. queryset[start_offset:stop] with start_offset < 0 raises ValueError("Negative indices are not allowed when slicing") — a cursor carrying a negative offset (crafted by clients or produced by the prev-direction math above when cursor.offset goes negative) returns a raw 500 instead of the 4xx the pagination contract expects, and since the endpoint merely toggles this path via the `optimized_pagination=true` query param, an authorized superuser hitting it gets an unhandled server error, not a validation rejection.

[BUG] The gating expression `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` dereferences `.member` without a None check. For any authenticated request where the user is not a member of the organization in the current context (e.g. superuser impersonation edge cases or member resolution failures that return None), `organization_context.member` is None and `.has_global_access` raises AttributeError, turning an otherwise valid GET /audit-logs with optimized_pagination=true into a 500 instead of falling back to the DateTimePaginator path or returning 403.

[BUG] The rewrite of OffsetPaginator.get_result clamps negative offsets to 0 for forward cursors, silently changing behavior, while the prev-cursor dedup check still compares len(results) against the unclamped `offset`. A forward cursor with a negative offset previously (in the old code) produced a Django slicing error surfaced as a 500; now it silently returns the first page of the dataset — the client believes it received page N but gets page 1 with no error, a silent-partial-success desync. Additionally, when `cursor.is_prev` and offset is negative (which this diff's sibling paginator can now emit), `offset` remains negative so `results[:-1]` and the `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` comparison slice/compute against a negative bound, dropping the wrong rows from the page.

[ADVISORY] The comment 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is factually false and is the load-bearing justification for the whole feature. The next maintainer who reads this comment will extend the negative-offset path (e.g. to the OffsetPaginator branch above, which was already partially rewired for it) trusting a claim the ORM violates; this is the exact comment that hides the P0 ValueError above from a future reviewer.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls int(math.floor(value)) but nothing in this diff verifies `math` is imported in paginator.py, and `self._is_asc(for_prev)` plus `self.desc`/`self.key` attribute lookups are not established by the BasePaginator contract for this subclass. Any GET on the audit-logs endpoint with optimized_pagination=true from a superuser that reaches build_cursor (the get_item_key is passed as `key=` to build_cursor) hits either NameError: math is not defined or AttributeError on `self.desc`/`self.key` — the entire optimized path 500s on the first real request, so the feature ships inert-but-crashing rather than working.

[ADVISORY] The new behavior is gated on a raw query parameter (`optimized_pagination=true`) combined with a permission check, with no feature flag, options entry, or way to disable it short of a code deploy, and the two paginators return structurally different cursor semantics for the same endpoint. Operators seeing 500s from the OptimizedCursorPaginator path (per the findings above) cannot turn it off without a deploy, and clients that fetch page 1 with the flag off and follow the returned cursor with the flag on (or vice versa) get mismatched cursor interpretation — silently wrong pages or errors — because cursor.value/offset semantics differ between DateTimePaginator and OptimizedCursorPaginator on the same endpoint.

[BUG] When cursor is None the paginator synthesizes Cursor(0, 0, 0), but when a client supplies a cursor whose value is 0 or unparseable, cursor_value falls back to 0 and build_queryset(0, ...) filters against a fabricated boundary value. A malformed or zero-valued cursor from the optimized path filters the queryset with key <= 0 (or >= 0 depending on direction) instead of rejecting the cursor, silently returning an empty or wrong page with HTTP 200 — the API reports success while the client's requested position is dropped.
